findings.title: Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() of contribution fields
findings.attack_path: Authenticated user POSTs preTax/afterTax/roth to /contributions; handler calls eval() directly on each raw body field before validation. Attacker submits a JS payload (e.g. a require('child_process') one-liner or a long-running loop) that executes in the Node process, yielding RCE, data theft from any collection, or process DoS.
findings.remediation: Replace eval() with parseInt(req.body.X, 10); reject non-numeric input. Never pass request data to eval/Function. Add a Content-Security-Policy and run the Node process with least privilege.

findings.title: NoSQL injection via unsanitized $where in allocations threshold
findings.attack_path: getByUserIdAndThreshold interpolates the raw threshold query param into a Mongo $where JavaScript string. Attacker requests /allocations/2?threshold=0';while(true){}'// to run arbitrary JS in the DB engine, exfiltrate other users' documents, or hang the mongod with an infinite loop.
findings.remediation: Drop $where entirely; use a numeric comparison query ({stocks: {$gt: parsedThreshold}}) after parseInt with bounds checking. Disable server-side JS in MongoDB (--noscripting).

findings.title: Passwords stored and compared in cleartext
findings.attack_path: addUser writes the raw password to the users collection and validateLogin compares with strict string equality (the bcrypt path is commented out). Any read of the users collection (via TM-002 injection, a DB compromise, or backups) discloses every plaintext credential, enabling account takeover and credential reuse against other systems.
findings.remediation: Hash passwords with bcrypt (genSalt + hashSync) on signup and compareSync on login. Re-hash existing credentials on next login and purge plaintext.

findings.title: IDOR: allocations exposed by user-controlled path parameter
findings.attack_path: displayAllocations reads userId from req.params, not the session, with only isLoggedIn applied. Any authenticated user enumerates /allocations/1, /allocations/2, ... to read every other user's allocation and joined profile name data. Sequential integer IDs make full enumeration trivial.
findings.remediation: Derive userId from req.session.userId; ignore the path parameter, or enforce an ownership/authorization check before returning records.

findings.title: Stored cross-user XSS via memos rendered with marked and autoescape disabled
findings.attack_path: POST /memos stores req.body.memo verbatim. getAllMemos returns ALL users' memos and memos.html renders each with {{ marked(doc.memo) }} while swig autoescape is globally disabled and marked 0.3.5 sanitize is weak. An attacker stores a script payload; it executes in every other user's (including admin's) session when they view /memos, stealing session cookies (which lack httpOnly) and enabling account takeover.
findings.remediation: Enable swig autoescape, upgrade marked and use a maintained HTML sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify server-side) on stored markdown output, and scope memo visibility per user.

findings.title: Missing function-level access control on admin benefits endpoints
findings.attack_path: /benefits routes apply only isLoggedIn; the isAdmin middleware is defined but commented out in index.js. Any authenticated non-admin user can GET /benefits to list all non-admin users and POST /benefits to modify any user's benefitStartDate, a privileged HR function.
findings.remediation: Add the isAdmin middleware to both /benefits routes (and any other privileged route); enforce role checks server-side on every privileged action.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in /research stock lookup
findings.attack_path: displayResearch builds url = req.query.url + req.query.symbol and calls needle.get on it, returning the response body to the client. An authenticated attacker sets url to an internal address or cloud metadata endpoint (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) to read internal services or steal instance credentials, or to file:// / localhost services.
findings.remediation: Remove the user-supplied url; use a fixed allowlisted upstream and pass only a validated symbol. If outbound fetch is required, enforce an allowlist of hosts/schemes and block link-local/private ranges.

findings.title: Hardcoded default/seed accounts with weak known passwords
findings.attack_path: db-reset.js seeds admin/Admin_123 (isAdmin true) plus user1/User1_123 and user2/User2_123 in plaintext. These public, predictable credentials let any attacker log in as admin immediately after a deploy/reset, gaining full privileged access.
findings.remediation: Remove seed accounts from production seeding, generate random admin credentials at provision time, force first-login password change, and never commit default passwords.

findings.title: Hardcoded session and crypto secrets in source
findings.attack_path: config/env/all.js commits cookieSecret, cryptoKey, and cryptoAlgo as literal strings. Anyone with repo access (public OWASP repo) knows the session-signing secret and can forge/tamper session cookies to impersonate arbitrary users including admin.
findings.remediation: Load all secrets from environment/secret manager, rotate the committed values, and fail startup if secrets are unset. Add the values to a secrets scanner denylist.

findings.title: TLS private key and certificate committed to the repository
findings.attack_path: artifacts/cert/server.key (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY) and server.crt are git-tracked. Any party with repo access holds the private key, enabling decryption of intercepted TLS traffic or impersonation of the server if this key is ever used in a real deployment.
findings.remediation: Remove the key from history (git filter-repo / BFG), revoke and reissue the certificate, and provision TLS material out-of-band via a secret store. Add *.key/*.pem to .gitignore.

findings.title: Insecure session cookies and session fixation on login
findings.attack_path: express-session is configured without httpOnly/secure cookie flags, uses the default in-memory store, and handleLoginRequest sets req.session.userId without calling req.session.regenerate(). An attacker who fixes or steals a pre-auth session id (XSS via TM-004, or network sniffing over cleartext HTTP) rides the session post-login to take over the account.
findings.remediation: Set cookie {httpOnly:true, secure:true, sameSite:'lax', maxAge}, use a persistent server-side session store, and regenerate the session id on every privilege change (login).

findings.title: Application served over cleartext HTTP only
findings.attack_path: server.js starts only http.createServer (the https path and HSTS are commented out). Credentials, session cookies, SSN/DOB/bank data, and admin actions all traverse the network in cleartext, exposing them to network-position attackers (MITM, sniffing).
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS (https server or a TLS-terminating proxy), enable HSTS via helmet, and redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Mark cookies secure once TLS is in place.

findings.title: Stored XSS / output-encoding gap on profile website link and fields
findings.attack_path: Profile fields are stored unescaped and rendered with swig autoescape disabled; website is HTML-encoded but then placed in an href URL context (firstNameSafeString in the anchor), the wrong encoding context. An attacker stores a javascript: URL or breaks out of an attribute to execute script in the victim's authenticated profile view, leading to session theft.
findings.remediation: Enable autoescape, apply context-correct encoding (encodeForURL for href, encodeForHTMLAttribute for attribute values), and validate the website field as an http(s) URL.

findings.title: Sensitive PII (SSN, DOB, bank account/routing) stored in cleartext
findings.attack_path: profile-dao.js writes ssn, dob, bankAcc, bankRouting to the users collection unencrypted (the crypto helpers are commented out). Any DB read (injection TM-002, backup theft, insider) discloses regulated financial PII for all users.
findings.remediation: Encrypt sensitive fields at rest (field-level encryption with a KMS-managed key), restrict read access, and mask values in UI/logs. Define retention and minimization.

findings.title: NoSQL operator injection on login username (auth bypass risk)
findings.attack_path: validateLogin passes req.body.userName straight into usersCol.findOne({userName}). Because body-parser.json is enabled, a JSON body like {"userName":{"$gt":""},"password":...} injects a Mongo operator object, returning an arbitrary user document and undermining the username lookup; combined with plaintext compare it aids enumeration/bypass.
findings.remediation: Coerce userName to a string and reject non-string types before querying; use a schema validator (e.g. express-mongo-sanitize) to strip $/dotted keys from request bodies.

findings.title: Missing CSRF protection on state-changing POST routes
findings.attack_path: csurf is imported but commented out in server.js, and cookies lack SameSite. A victim authenticated to NodeGoat who visits an attacker page is forced to submit POST /profile, /contributions, /benefits, or /memos cross-site, altering their data or planting stored XSS without consent.
findings.remediation: Enable CSRF tokens (csurf or equivalent) on all state-changing routes and set SameSite on session cookies.

findings.title: Outdated and vulnerable dependencies / EOL runtime
findings.attack_path: package.json pins mongodb ^2.x (legacy $where JS exec), marked 0.3.5 (known XSS bypasses), swig ^1.4.2 (unmaintained), bcrypt-nodejs 0.0.3 (deprecated), and the Dockerfile uses node:12-alpine (EOL). Known CVEs in these components widen the exploit surface and prevent timely patching.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to maintained majors (mongodb 5+, a maintained markdown+sanitizer, supported templating), move to a supported Node LTS base image, and add automated dependency scanning (npm audit / Snyk) in CI.

findings.title: Regular-expression denial of service in bank routing validation
findings.attack_path: handleProfileUpdate tests bankRouting against /([0-9]+)+\#/ which has nested quantifiers causing catastrophic backtracking. A POST /profile with a long all-digit string and no # pins a CPU core, and because the runtime is single-threaded the whole server stalls (DoS).
findings.remediation: Replace with a linear regex (e.g. /^[0-9]+#$/), bound input length, and/or run validation with a timeout.

findings.title: Open redirect via /learn url parameter
findings.attack_path: GET /learn does res.redirect(req.query.url) with no validation. An attacker crafts /learn?url=https://evil.example to bounce victims off the trusted domain for phishing or token leakage via redirect.
findings.remediation: Redirect only to a server-side allowlist of relative paths/known hosts; reject absolute external URLs.

findings.title: Username enumeration through distinct login error messages
findings.attack_path: handleLoginRequest returns 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' (the unified-message fix is commented out). An attacker harvests valid usernames by observing which message comes back, narrowing targets for brute force/credential stuffing.
findings.remediation: Return a single generic 'Invalid username and/or password' message for all auth failures and add per-account/IP rate limiting.

findings.title: Missing security response headers (helmet disabled)
findings.attack_path: All helmet middleware (frameguard, CSP, HSTS, noSniff) and x-powered-by removal are commented out in server.js. Absent CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options amplifies XSS, enables clickjacking of authenticated pages, and discloses the Express stack.
findings.remediation: Enable helmet with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, frameguard, HSTS, and noSniff; disable x-powered-by.

findings.title: Weak password policy at signup
findings.attack_path: validateSignup accepts any password matching /^.{1,20}$/ (a single character passes); the stronger-policy regex is commented out. Combined with no rate limiting, accounts are trivially brute-forced or set with guessable passwords.
findings.remediation: Enforce minimum length and complexity (e.g. 8+ chars with mixed classes) server-side, check against breached-password lists, and add login rate limiting.

findings.title: MongoDB deployed without authentication on shared network
findings.attack_path: docker-compose.yml runs mongo:4.4 with no credentials and the app connects via mongodb://mongo:27017/nodegoat (no auth string). Any workload that reaches the Mongo port on the compose/host network reads or writes every collection, including cleartext credentials and PII, without authentication.
findings.remediation: Enable MongoDB auth (SCRAM users, --auth), supply credentials via secrets, restrict the DB to an internal network only, and enable TLS for the DB connection.

findings.title: Log injection (CRLF) via unsanitized username in login logging
findings.attack_path: On an invalid-user login, console.log prints the raw userName (the ESAPI/CRLF-strip fix is commented out). An attacker embeds CRLF and fake log lines in the username to forge log entries, hide activity, or poison downstream log parsers, undermining accountability.
findings.remediation: Strip/encode CR/LF and control characters from user input before logging, or use a structured logger that escapes field values.

findings.title: Verbose error page leaks stack traces
findings.attack_path: The error handler renders the full error object (including message and stack via the template) to the client. Triggering an exception reveals file paths, library versions, and internal logic that aid an attacker in crafting further exploits.
findings.remediation: Return a generic error page to clients; log details server-side only. Differentiate production vs development error verbosity.
